correctness.rationale: For each integer k≥2 and n in {k²−1,k²}, capacity k² fixes the sum of truncation and overlap multiplicities to 0 or 1. Legally timed sources exclude a singleton final neighborhood overlapping the interior of another radius interval. The remaining configurations are unique ordered interval tilings, one-end clipping or one-endpoint overlap, with each configuration meeting the source distance constraints and covering the graph. Bijections give all four totals and four redundant subcounts, including k=2 cycle C3; independent round-by-round direct brute force for k=2..4 and a separate constructive enumeration for k=2..6 replay successfully. Finite checks corroborate rather than establish the all-k claim.

value.rationale: The recent graph-burning literature explicitly identifies last-ignition redundancy as mathematically significant (e.g. for burning numbers of graph products), and points out its absence for square-length paths. Determining all legally timed optimum strategies one vertex below that sharp capacity boundary is a motivated stability and emergence problem. The all-k one-defect rigidity, four factorial enumerators and exact redundant-source fractions resolve this natural question, extending known length-only formulas in a way that an extremal minimum does not imply.
